alt: Interactive: choosing a variance estimator shows its standard error, interval and p-value for the same coefficient, what it assumes, and the code in R, Python and Stata.
note: Ratios are relative to the IID standard error. Verdicts follow the design: the policy is assigned to states and state shocks persist across years.

options.assumes: Every observation is an independent draw with the same error variance. Ten people in the same state and year, and the same state in consecutive years, are treated as unrelated.

code.python: pf.feols("y ~ d | state + year", data=panel, vcov="iid")
code.r: feols(y ~ d | state + year, data = panel, vcov = "iid")

options.label: IID (fixest 0.13+ default)

options.assumes: Error variances may differ across observations, but no two observations are correlated. Heteroskedasticity is not the problem in this design, so the number barely moves.

code.python: pf.feols("y ~ d | state + year", data=panel, vcov="hetero")
code.r: feols(y ~ d | state + year, data = panel, vcov = "hetero")
code.stata: reghdfe y d, absorb(state year) vce(robust)

options.label: HC1

options.assumes: People in the same state and year may be correlated in any way; a state's consecutive years are independent. Persistent state shocks and a policy that stays on violate this.

code.python: pf.feols("y ~ d | state + year", data=panel, vcov={"CRV1": "state_year"})
code.r: feols(y ~ d | state + year, data = panel, vcov = ~state^year)
code.stata:
egen state_year = group(state year)
reghdfe y d, absorb(state year) vce(cluster state_year)

options.label: Cluster by state-year

options.assumes: Observations may be correlated within a state across all years, and within a year across all states. Valid here; the year dimension adds little because year shocks are absorbed by the fixed effects.

code.python: pf.feols("y ~ d | state + year", data=panel, vcov={"CRV1": "state+year"})
code.r: feols(y ~ d | state + year, data = panel, vcov = ~state + year)
code.stata: reghdfe y d, absorb(state year) vce(cluster state year)

options.label: Two-way: state and year

options.assumes: Observations within a state may be correlated in any way across people and years; states are independent. The policy was assigned to states and the shocks persist within them: this is the design.

code.python: pf.feols("y ~ d | state + year", data=panel, vcov={"CRV1": "state"})
code.r: feols(y ~ d | state + year, data = panel, vcov = ~state)
code.stata: reghdfe y d, absorb(state year) vce(cluster state)

options.label: Cluster by state (fixest <= 0.12 default)

options.assumes: Correlation across all states within a year and across years up to the lag, through the period sums of the scores. Built for panels with long time dimensions and common shocks; 20 years is short for it.

code.python: pf.feols("y ~ d | state + year", data=panel, vcov="DK", vcov_kwargs={"time_id": "year", "lag": 4})
code.r: feols(y ~ d | state + year, data = panel, vcov = DK(4) ~ year)
code.stata:
xtset state year
xtscc y d i.year, fe lag(4)

options.label: Driscoll-Kraay, 4 lags

source: Simulation: sim.R with R fixest (this chapter); no survey data
subtitle: The opening panel: 50 states, 20 years, a placebo policy with a true effect of zero. Choose an estimator.
title: One coefficient, one argument, six answers
